title: Hunchboard provocations and priority strips
high_level_summary: Loose synthesis of customer hunches, grouped by fragility and cost to fix, with a handful of low-risk experiments to run during April sprint. Emphasis on runtime edgecases (kv cache misses, burst latency) and console UX friction when pinning model versions.
priority_actions: Run 2-week A/B of prefix cache warmup heuristic (config flag + telemetry) against 5 mid-market customers to measure token-savings and 95th pct latency
Ship console tweak: expose 'pin-to-version' warning with suggested fallback profiles (small UI patch, docs + telemetry) — low dev effort
Create short-runbook for SRE on model-fallback incidents: step checklist, triage tags, and automated rollback script entrypoint
Prototype lightweight per-route batching suggestion in Optimize: show savings estimate for enabling batching@500ms window
body:
Context and purpose:
- Quick capture after customer calls (Mar 1–Mar 3) + product-sprint brainstorm (Mar 4). Not exhaustive — raw field notes that should feed into a baked roadmap doc later.

Group A: latency fragility (high customer pain, medium engineering cost)
- Observed: customers running chat-like flows report sporadic 95th pct spikes when context length grows beyond 4k tokens. Several incidents correlated with heavy cache churn (many short sessions with unique prefixes).
- Customer quote: 'We see tail latency every morning at 09:00 when usage spikes — it kills our SLA.' — mid-market fintech.
- Hunch: default KV eviction + cold prefix behaviour causes repeated KV recompute, which increases per-token cost and latency.
- Quick probes: (1) simulate high churn with our staging workload; (2) enable prefix-warm heuristic on one tenant and see token-reuse; (3) add TTL-based soft eviction.
- Risks: changes touch runtime cache policy; rollback should be straightforward if feature-flagged.

Group B: pinned model UX and accidental rollouts (high frequency, low-friction fix)
- Observed: support log shows ~14 tickets/month where customers thought they'd pinned a model, but console routing fell back silently during capacity events. Leads to confusion and trust loss.
- Customer quote: 'We thought we were pinned to v1.2 but traffic moved to the cheaper variant without notice.' — platform team at a SaaS customer.
- Proposed microfix: add persistent 'pinned model' indicator, and a short modal that explains fallback policy and offers an opt-in to strict pin (with capacity warning). Update API docs with explicit examples.
- Impact: improves trust; trivial console + docs work; could reduce support tickets and required handoffs.

Group C: billing/observability mismatch (medium pain, policy + infra work)
- Observed: teams report token cost differences between SDK-level token counts and billing console. Root cause: post-processing/structured output truncation and streaming accounting differences.
- Ask: reconcile token accounting in docs + add a debug endpoint that returns both 'charged_tokens' and 'computed_tokens' for a request.
- Consideration: exposing extra fields increases surface area for customers but will dramatically lower 'why did my bill spike' tickets.

Group D: feature requests & nice-to-haves (low friction, high delight)
- Per-route quality metrics: customers want a small panel that surfaces per-prompt eval metrics (BLEU/ROUGE or custom eval outcome) to quickly catch regressions after rollouts.
- Config-as-code for rollout policies: a YAML snippet export/import that SRE and platform teams can version.
- Embedding stability toggles: allow customers to pick embedding normalization presets to avoid drift after minor model updates.

Mini-prioritized backlog (short descriptions + why):
1) Pinning transparency modal (low dev, high PR impact) — reduces customer confusion and support volume.
2) Prefix-warm heuristic experiment (medium dev, high potential cost reduction) — run controlled A/B with 5 tenants.
3) Billing debug endpoint and docs (low-to-medium dev, immediate support savings) — add to API protos.
4) Per-route quality panel MVP (low dev prototype as hackday project) — gather interest.
5) Opt-in strict-pin policy for enterprise (policy + capacity planning; coordinate with Dedicated sales).

Operational notes and next steps:
- Owners: Priya to coordinate experiments with Applied ML; Ethan to scope console mock and PR; Lena to draft billing debug API; Noah to schedule customer pilots and capture telemetry schema.
- Metrics to capture: 95th latency, median token cost per request, percent of requests served by fallback variant, support ticket count related to 'pinning' and 'billing explanation'.
- Timeline: aim to land UI modal and billing debug endpoint as quick wins in Apr sprint; start prefix-warm experiment April 10; measure for 4 weeks.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How much memory overhead will prefix-warm introduce at large scale? Need infra estimate.
- Is there an acceptable UI wording that balances transparency vs. scaring customers about capacity limits? Quick copy loop recommended.
- For billing debug endpoint, what PII/PI data boundaries apply? Loop in security/compliance.

Attachments / raw snippets captured during calls:
- Slack excerpt: "we keep seeing the 'model fallback' banner but can't tell which requests were affected" — customer SRE.
- Ticket example (internal): RED-4926 referenced above — shows steps to reproduce pin confusion.

Quick wins for next two weeks (ordered):
1) Console: add small 'pinned' badge + hover text (Ethan)
2) API: add 'debug_tokens' flag returning charged vs computed (Lena)
3) Docs: short FAQ 'Why did my model change?' and a canned support response template (Priya)

Notes to product leads:
- These are exploratory hunches; this doc should be used to seed a more formal requirement doc if we see signal from experiments. Recommend shipping UI + docs first and only change runtime cache policy after pilot data.
- Coordinate with Dedicated/Private teams before enabling any strict-pin policy — capacity and SLA commitments differ.

End of notes.
